completed.name: DLMF.Hypergeometric.genHG_dougall_5F4_terminating
completed.doc: Dougall terminating 5F4, with all removable cases retained by finite products.

completed.name: DLMF.Struve.lommelCapital_ode
completed.doc:
The capital Lommel function solves the inhomogeneous Bessel equation throughout the slit
plane, including exceptional parameters filled in by the parameter limit.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Hypergeometric.dougall_unitD_classical_limit
newHelpers.doc:
The normalized polynomial unit-Bailey factor has the expected classical limit. Bailey’s
cleared identity avoids square-root choices in the very-well-poised pair.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Hypergeometric.dougall_unitD_factorial_classical_limit
newHelpers.doc:
Dividing the unit-Bailey factor by the factorial q-Pochhammer gives its classical
coefficient normalization.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Hypergeometric.dougall_classical_unit_eq
newHelpers.doc:
The classical unit factor equals the usual half-parameter Pochhammer quotient whenever
the lower half-parameter is regular.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Hypergeometric.dougall_qPochhammer_eventually_ne_zero
newHelpers.doc:
A finite q-Pochhammer product stays nonzero near the classical limit when its limiting
rising factorial is nonzero.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Hypergeometric.dougall_qpow_params
newHelpers.doc:
The lower parameters and argument in the rational q-Dougall sum become sums and
differences of classical exponents.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Hypergeometric.dougall_qterm_classical_limit
newHelpers.doc:
Each rational terminating q-Dougall summand tends to the corresponding classical
very-well-poised `₅F₄` coefficient.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Hypergeometric.dougall7_last_den_ne
newHelpers.doc:
The balancing relation reflects the last denominator Pochhammer into the regular lower
parameter paired with `f`, so that denominator stays nonzero.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Hypergeometric.dougall_eventually_not_neg_nat_at
newHelpers.doc:
On a punctured neighborhood of any complex point, the nonpositive integers are avoided.
This combines their discreteness with openness of their complement.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Hypergeometric.dougall_poch_continuous
newHelpers.doc: A fixed rising factorial is a polynomial in its parameter, hence continuous.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Hypergeometric.dougall7_product_eval
newHelpers.doc:
Under the Dougall balance, Pochhammer reflection turns the Whipple prefactor times
Saalschütz’s value into the finite `₇F₆` product.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Hypergeometric.dougall7_generic
newHelpers.doc:
Whipple’s terminating transformation and Saalschütz’s sum prove finite Dougall when the
parameter canceled from the transformed `₄F₃` is regular.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Hypergeometric.dougall7_difference_continuous
newHelpers.doc:
The difference of the finite Dougall sum and its product is continuous in a varying
parameter, because the displayed denominators are nonzero at the reference point.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Hypergeometric.continuous_regularized1F2_one
newHelpers.doc: The regularized `₁F₂(1;b,c;q)` is jointly continuous in its lower parameters and argument.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Struve.lommelNumerator_joint_continuous
newHelpers.doc:
The Lommel cancellation numerator is jointly continuous in degree and argument on the
slit plane.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Struve.lommel_eventually_regular
newHelpers.doc: All sufficiently close punctured degree parameters are regular.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Struve.lommelCapital_parameter_locallyUniform
newHelpers.doc:
Pole cancellation is continuous jointly in degree and argument, hence the parameter limit
is locally uniform on the slit plane.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Weierstrass.HalfPeriods.inv_sin_sq_eq_exp
newHelpers.doc: The reciprocal sine square in exponential coordinates, away from its poles.

newHelpers.name: tendstoLocallyUniformlyOn_of_joint_continuousAt
newHelpers.doc: Joint continuity along a parameter slice gives locally uniform convergence to that slice.

newHelpers.name: tendstoLocallyUniformlyOn_of_local_extension
newHelpers.doc:
A local continuous extension upgrades an identified pointwise limit to locally uniform
convergence, for any nontrivial parameter filter approaching the extension point.

reusableExistingHelpers.name: DLMF.QHypergeometric.tendsto_cpow_increment
reusableExistingHelpers.doc: The normalized principal-power increment tends to its exponent as the real base approaches one.

reusableExistingHelpers.name: DLMF.QHypergeometric.tendsto_qPochhammer_normalized
reusableExistingHelpers.doc: A normalized finite q-Pochhammer symbol tends to the ordinary rising factorial.

reusableExistingHelpers.name: DLMF.QHypergeometric.tendsto_qPochhammerList_ratio
reusableExistingHelpers.doc: Equal-length finite products have a classical ratio limit with no residual power of one minus q.

material_gaps_and_conventions: Native definitions, aliases, independent integral/series realizations, selected continuations and theorem-only bridges are distinguished; totalized operations are not treated as analytic continuation.
Kelvin functions/continuous phases, cylindrical-Bessel continuous modulus/phase constructions and a principal Mathieu exponent selector remain named-family gaps.
General Lamé Ec/Es are real-variable choices; complex polynomial Lamé objects are independently constructed finite sums and do not provide the general complex continuation.

Primary Mathieu/Lamé/spheroidal existence specifications have compiled no-sorryAx audits; noninteger Mathieu, Heun disk/Stieltjes, Lambert branch choices and Ince specifications retain their individual admission qualifications.

Gamma continued-fraction data with finitely listed coefficients, Coulomb transitionA/B and spheroidal prolate/oblate coefficients do not define the intended all-order sequences beyond their explicitly populated indices.
Spheroidal Qs requires a nonzero forward-recursion matching coefficient; totalized division does not remove this obstruction.
Narayana N(0,0) is zero locally versus the DLMF empty-path convention one; existing path theorems restrict positive length.
The local Weierstrass nTupleConst intentionally corrects the printed23.10.14 product, excluding only the origin pair rather than every diagonal pair.
AGM c_n conventions in19.8and22.20 agree on positive ordered real data; the additional gap is complex branch tracking.
airyTerminator on the logarithmic cover is exp(z) times the8.22 terminant F_p, hence the10.17 G_p normalization.
Definitions of numerical methods and application objects are descriptive only; decimal values, graphical claims and implementation-only helpers are excluded.
